list_actors.title: List Actors
list_actors.description: List the Actors the account has created or used, newest-created last unless `desc` is set. Each item has id, name, username and run stats. Set `my` to see only your own Actors; to find public Actors you have not used, use search_store_actors.

my.description: If `true` then the returned list only contains Actors owned by the user. The default value is `false`.

offset.description: Number of items to skip at the start, for paging (default 0).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default and maximum 1000 for most lists).

desc.description: Sort newest first (by createdAt / startedAt) instead of oldest first.

sort_by.description: Sort by `createdAt` (default) or `stats.lastRunStartedAt` for the most recently run Actors.

output.description: A page of Actors: total, offset, limit, count and items.

create_actor.title: Create an Actor
create_actor.description: Create a new Actor in the account. Give it at least a `name`; `versions` holds the source (inline files, Git repo, tarball or Gist). Build it with build_actor before running it. Returns the Actor object with its id.

name.description: Actor name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the account, e.g. `my-scraper`.

title.description: Human-readable title shown in Console and Store.

description.description: Short description shown in Console and Store.

is_public.description: Publish the Actor to Apify Store (default false, private).

seo_description.description: Description for search engines, 140-156 characters recommended.

restart_on_error.description: Restart runs automatically when they fail.

versions.description: Version objects: {versionNumber: "0.0", sourceType: SOURCE_FILES|GIT_REPO|TARBALL|GITHUB_GIST, buildTag: "latest", sourceFiles: [{name, format: TEXT|BASE64, content}], gitRepoUrl, tarballUrl, gitHubGistUrl, envVars: [{name, value, isSecret}]}.

actor_standby.description: Standby mode configuration: {isEnabled, desiredRequestsPerActorRun, maxRequestsPerActorRun, idleTimeoutSecs, build, memoryMbytes}.

default_build.description: Default build tag or number for runs, e.g. `latest`.

default_memory_mbytes.description: Default run memory in megabytes (power of 2, at least 128).

get_actor.title: Get an Actor
get_actor.description: Get an Actor's full record: name, title, description, versions, default run options, tagged builds (taggedBuilds.latest.buildId), pricing and stats. Works for your own Actors and public Store Actors.

is_public.description: Whether the Actor is published in Apify Store.

restart_on_error.description: Restart runs automatically when they fail.

tagged_builds.description: Map of tag name to {buildId} (or null to remove the tag), e.g. {"beta": {"buildId": "abc"}}.

actor_permission_level.description: Permission level the Actor runs with.

default_build.description: Default build tag or number for runs.

actor_id.description: Actor id, or the owner's username and the Actor name joined by a tilde, e.g. `apify~web-scraper`.

validate_actor_input.title: Validate Actor input

build_actor.title: Build an Actor

run_actor.title: Run an Actor
run_actor.description: Start an Actor run and return at once with the run object (id, status, defaultDatasetId, defaultKeyValueStoreId). actor_id.description: Actor id, or the owner's username and the Actor name joined by a tilde, e.g. `apify~web-scraper`.

timeout.description: Run timeout in seconds. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

memory.description: Memory limit in megabytes, a power of 2 of at least 128. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

max_items.description: For pay-per-result Actors: the most dataset items you are willing to be charged for. It does not cap what the Actor returns.

max_total_charge_usd.description: Cap on the total cost of the run in USD, across all pricing models.

restart_on_error.description: Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.

build.description: Build tag or number to use, e.g. `latest` or `0.1.23`. Defaults to the configured build.

wait_for_finish.description: Seconds to wait for the job to finish before responding, 0-60 (default 0). Poll again if the status is still not terminal.

force_permission_level.description: Overrides the Actor's permission level for this specific run. If you don't specify this parameter, the Actor uses its configured default permission level.

input.description: The Actor input as a JSON object, matching the Actor's input schema (see get_actor or the Actor's Store page). Omit to use the Actor's default or example input.

run_actor_sync.title: Run an Actor and get its output
run_actor_sync.description: Run an Actor, wait for it to finish (at most 300 seconds) and return the record it stored under OUTPUT (or `output_record_key`) in its default key-value store. Times out with 408 on longer runs; use run_actor for those. The input is sent as the run's INPUT record.

actor_id.description: Actor id, or the owner's username and the Actor name joined by a tilde, e.g. `apify~web-scraper`.

output_record_key.description: Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.

timeout.description: Run timeout in seconds. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

memory.description: Memory limit in megabytes, a power of 2 of at least 128. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

max_items.description: For pay-per-result Actors: the most dataset items you are willing to be charged for. It does not cap what the Actor returns.

max_total_charge_usd.description: Cap on the total cost of the run in USD, across all pricing models.

restart_on_error.description: Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.

build.description: Build tag or number to use, e.g. `latest` or `0.1.23`. Defaults to the configured build.

input.description: The Actor input as a JSON object, matching the Actor's input schema (see get_actor or the Actor's Store page). Omit to use the Actor's default or example input.

output.description: The run's output record, in whatever shape the Actor stored it.

run_actor_sync_get_dataset_items.title: Run an Actor and get its dataset items
run_actor_sync_get_dataset_items.description: Run an Actor, wait for it to finish (at most 300 seconds) and return the items from its default dataset: the usual way to get scraper results in one call. actor_id.description: Actor id, or the owner's username and the Actor name joined by a tilde, e.g. `apify~web-scraper`.

timeout.description: Run timeout in seconds. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

memory.description: Memory limit in megabytes, a power of 2 of at least 128. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

restart_on_error.description: Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.

build.description: Build tag or number to use, e.g. `latest` or `0.1.23`. Defaults to the configured build.

format.description: Output format: json (default), jsonl, csv, html, xml or rss. Non-JSON formats come back as text.

clean.description: If `true` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character). The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.

offset.description: Number of items to skip at the start, for paging (default 0).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default: all items, subject to the response size limit).

fields.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects. output_fields.description: A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter. For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.

omit.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.

unwind.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object. If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.

flatten.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures. For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`. The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.

desc.description: Return items in reverse order, last stored first.

delimiter.description: A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B` for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).

skip_hidden.description: If `true` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.

skip_empty.description: If `true` then empty items are skipped from the output. Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.

view.description: Name of a dataset view from the dataset schema, which picks and orders fields for display.

input.description: The Actor input as a JSON object, matching the Actor's input schema (see get_actor or the Actor's Store page). Omit to use the Actor's default or example input.

output.description: The dataset items (text for non-JSON formats).

task_id.description: Task id, or the owner's username and task name joined by a tilde, e.g. `janedoe~my-task`.

timeout.description: Run timeout in seconds. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

memory.description: Memory limit in megabytes, a power of 2 of at least 128. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

max_items.description: For pay-per-result Actors: the most dataset items you are willing to be charged for. It does not cap what the Actor returns.

max_total_charge_usd.description: Cap on the total cost of the run in USD, across all pricing models.

restart_on_error.description: Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.

build.description: Build tag or number to use, e.g. `latest` or `0.1.23`. Defaults to the configured build.

wait_for_finish.description: Seconds to wait for the job to finish before responding, 0-60 (default 0). Poll again if the status is still not terminal.

input.description: Input fields that override the task's saved input for this run only.

run_task_sync.title: Run a task and get its output
run_task_sync.description: Run a task, wait for it to finish (at most 300 seconds) and return the record it stored under OUTPUT (or `output_record_key`). Fields in `input` override the saved input. Use run_task for longer jobs.

task_id.description: Task id, or the owner's username and task name joined by a tilde, e.g. `janedoe~my-task`.

timeout.description: Run timeout in seconds. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

memory.description: Memory limit in megabytes, a power of 2 of at least 128. Defaults to the Actor or task configuration.

max_total_charge_usd.description: Cap on the total cost of the run in USD, across all pricing models.

restart_on_error.description: Determines whether the run will be restarted if it fails.

build.description: Build tag or number to use, e.g. `latest` or `0.1.23`. Defaults to the configured build.

output_record_key.description: Key of the record from the run's default key-value store to return in the response. Defaults to `OUTPUT`. Actors aren't required to store a record under this key, so if it doesn't exist the response contains no data.

input.description: Input fields that override the task's saved input for this run only.

format.description: Output format: json (default), jsonl, csv, html, xml or rss. Non-JSON formats come back as text.

clean.description: If `true` then the API endpoint returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (i.e. fields starting with the # character). The `clean` parameter is just a shortcut for `skipHidden=true` and `skipEmpty=true` parameters.

offset.description: Number of items to skip at the start, for paging (default 0).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default: all items, subject to the response size limit).

fields.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be picked from the items, only these fields will remain in the resulting record objects. Note that the fields in the outputted items are sorted the same way as they are specified in the `fields` query parameter. You can use this feature to effectively fix the output format.

output_fields.description: A comma-separated list of output field names that positionally rename the fields specified in the `fields` parameter. For example, `?fields=headline,url&outputFields=title,link` renames `headline` to `title` and `url` to `link` in the output.

omit.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.

unwind.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object. If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.

flatten.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures. desc.description: Return items in reverse order, last stored first.

delimiter.description: A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B` for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).

get_run.description: Get an Actor run: status (READY, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, TIMED-OUT, ABORTED...), status message, timing, usage and cost, and the ids of its default dataset, key-value store and request queue. Pass wait_for_finish to block up to 60 s for completion.

abort_run.title: Abort a run
abort_run.description: Stop a running Actor run. With `gracefully` the Actor gets 30 seconds to persist state, which lets it be resurrected later. Returns the run with status ABORTING or ABORTED.

metamorph_run.description: Transform a running Actor run into a run of another Actor with a new input, keeping the same run id and default storages; the new input is stored as INPUT-METAMORPH-1. Usually called by an Actor on its own run.

omit.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be omitted from the items.

unwind.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should be unwound, in order which they should be processed. Each field should be either an array or an object. If the field is an array then every element of the array will become a separate record and merged with parent object.

flatten.description: A comma-separated list of fields which should transform nested objects into flat structures. For example, with `flatten="foo"` the object `{"foo":{"bar": "hello"}}` is turned into `{"foo.bar": "hello"}`. The original object with properties is replaced with the flattened object.

desc.description: Return items in reverse order, last stored first.

delimiter.description: A delimiter character for CSV files, only used if `format=csv`. You might need to URL-encode the character (e.g. use `%09` for tab or `%3B` for semicolon). The default delimiter is a simple comma (`,`).

skip_header_row.description: If `true` then header row in the `csv` format is skipped.

skip_hidden.description: If `true` then hidden fields are skipped from the output, i.e. fields starting with the `#` character.

skip_empty.description: If `true` then empty items are skipped from the output. Note that if used, the results might contain less items than the limit value.

view.description: Name of a dataset view from the dataset schema, which picks and orders fields for display.

output.description: The dataset items (text for non-JSON formats).

push_dataset_items.title: Push dataset items
push_dataset_items.description: Append items to a dataset. Pass a list of JSON objects (or a single object). Items are immutable once stored; the payload may be at most 9 MB.

dataset_id.description: Dataset id, or `username~dataset-name`. A run's default dataset id is its defaultDatasetId.

output.description: Nothing; Apify answers 201 with an empty body.

get_dataset_statistics.title: Get dataset statistics
get_dataset_statistics.description: Get per-field statistics for a dataset, such as how many items have each field and how many are empty.

dataset_id.description: Dataset id, or `username~dataset-name`. A run's default dataset id is its defaultDatasetId.

create_request_queue.title: Create a request queue
create_request_queue.description: Create a request queue of URLs to crawl. With a `name` it is kept indefinitely and an existing queue of that name is returned instead; without one it expires with data retention.

get_request_queue.title: Get a request queue

list_requests.description: List the requests in a queue, paging with `cursor`, optionally only locked or pending ones.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return (default and maximum 10000).

filter.description: Filter requests by their state. Possible values are `locked` and `pending`. You can combine multiple values separated by commas, which will mean the union of these filters – requests matching any of the specified states will be returned. (Not compatible with deprecated `exclusiveStartId` parameter.)

add_request.title: Add a request
add_request.description: Add one URL request to a queue, at the end or the head (`forefront`). A request whose unique_key is already in the queue is not added again; the response says whether it was already present or handled.

batch_delete_requests.description: Delete up to 25 requests from a queue in one call, each identified by its id or uniqueKey.

requests.description: Requests to delete, each {id} or {uniqueKey}, up to 25.

get_request.description: Get one request from a queue: url, uniqueKey, method, userData, retry count and handledAt.

unlock_requests.description: Release every lock the client (identified by `client_key`) holds in a queue.

client_key.description: Identifier (1-32 chars) of the client using the queue, so Apify can tell whether several clients accessed it and which one holds locks.
